RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 15

A single-gender panel is not evidence of discrimination. In the civil service, panel compositions depend largely on availability, seniority, and relevant departmental roles. Both you and the appointee were strong finalists; her experience leading international projects and her interview performance likely tipped the balance according to the role's specific selection criteria.

Raising the panel's gender without concrete evidence would be viewed as an unsubstantiated accusation and could severely damage your professional standing within the civil service. Two weeks is also a common government administrative timeframe, so simply send a polite follow-up requesting your competency scores and constructive feedback to understand the decision.
